interest: Docket summarizing every Japanese cabinet crisis and assassination of 1930–39 in one sequence.
overview: This file comprises the Department of State's 26-page 'List of Papers' (docket sheet and purport list) for decimal file 894.002 (Political Affairs., Japan, Cabinet. Ministry), cataloguing incoming and outgoing diplomatic correspondence, memoranda, intelligence reports, and cross-references from October 1930 through December 1939. The register chronicles a decade of political volatility and cabinet turnover in pre-WWII Japan, documenting the aftermath of the attempted assassination of Prime Minister Osachi Hamaguchi, the brief cabinets of Reijiro Wakatsuki and Tsuyoshi Inukai (culminating in the May 15, 1932 incident), the national unity cabinets of Makoto Saito and Keisuke Okada, the February 26, 1936 military uprising, and the subsequent administrations of Koki Hirota, Senjuro Hayashi, Fumimaro Konoe, Kiichiro Hiranuma, and Nobuyuki Abe. Through hundreds of numbered entries, the document records ministerial appointments, resignations, party politics between the Minseito and Seiyukai, the increasing political veto exercised by the Imperial Army and Navy, bureaucratic friction over foreign policy and China administration, and the diplomatic impact of major events such as the Manchurian Incident, the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War, and the 1939 Soviet-German Non-Aggression Pact.

subfiles.about: A continuous 26-page Department of State register and purport list cataloguing diplomatic communications, memoranda, and cross-references regarding the Japanese Cabinet and Ministry from October 1930 to December 1939.
subfiles.summary: This 26-page docket register serves as the complete administrative finding aid and purport sheet for State Department decimal file 894.002 between 1930 and 1939. It records hundreds of dispatches, telegrams, and cross-references documenting frequent Japanese cabinet changes, ministerial appointments, and political crises from the Hamaguchi administration through the Abe government. Major historical events indexed include the shootings of Prime Ministers Hamaguchi and Inukai, the February 26, 1936 incident, military pressure on cabinet formation, and the political fallout from the China conflict and the German-Soviet pact.
